paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We compare error rate (one minus accuracy), computation cost, and memory usage across our approach and baselines when fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks. MTL-FT refers to first fine-tuning a shared LoRA on all the datasets, and then fine-tuning the low-rank adapter on each dataset, while Full FT refers to full fine-tuning of the entire model. Our approach boosts the test accuracy of QLoRA by 10\% on average, only incurring 8\% additional computation and 9 GB more memory. It performs on par with the best baseline with 45\% less FLOPs.

The horizontal axis displays six distinct methods labeled "Full FT", "TAG", "LoRA", "MTL-FT", "QLoRA", and "Ours", arranged in a left-to-right sequence that appears to follow an approximate alphabetical order of their labels. The vertical axis represents the number of FLOPs on a logarithmic scale, spanning from 10^18 to 10^20, with tick marks and grid lines indicating equal logarithmic intervals. The bars corresponding to "Full FT", "TAG", "LoRA", and "MTL-FT" are colored orange, while the bar for "Ours" is colored green, suggesting a visual distinction between the baseline methods and the proposed approach. The bar heights indicate relative computation costs, with "Full FT" being the tallest at approximately 10^20 FLOPs, followed by "TAG" and "LoRA" at similar high levels, then "MTL-FT" at a lower level, "QLoRA" at an even lower level, and "Ours" being the shortest at approximately 10^19 FLOPs. The chart does not include any additional annotations, error bars, or legends beyond the bar colors and axis labels.
model_annotations.English: This bar chart, titled "QLoRA," illustrates the number of FLOPs (floating-point operations) required for various fine-tuning methods when applied to Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks. The horizontal axis displays six distinct methods labeled "Full FT," "TAG," "LoRA," "MTL-FT," "QLoRA," and "Ours," arranged from left to right in descending order of computational cost. The vertical axis, labeled "# FLOPs," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^18 to 10^20, with tick marks at intervals of 10^18, 10^19, and 10^20. Each bar represents the total FLOPs for its respective method: the "Full FT" bar is the tallest, reaching approximately 1.0 x 10^20 FLOPs; the "TAG" bar is slightly shorter, at about 8.0 x 10^19 FLOPs; the "LoRA" bar is next at roughly 7.0 x 10^19 FLOPs; the "MTL-FT" bar is at approximately 6.0 x 10^19 FLOPs; the "QLoRA" bar is at about 5.0 x 10^19 FLOPs; and the "Ours" bar, colored green, is the shortest at approximately 4.0 x 10^19 FLOPs. All bars except "Ours" are orange, while "Ours" is distinctly green, visually emphasizing its lower computational cost relative to the other methods. The chart does not include error rate or memory usage data, focusing solely on FLOPs.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm mit dem Titel „QLoRA“ visualisiert die Anzahl an FLOPs (Floating Point Operations) für verschiedene Fine-tuning-Methoden, die auf einem Llama-3-8B-Modell angewendet wurden. Die x-Achse listet die Methoden in alphabetischer Reihenfolge: „Full FT“, „TAG“, „LoRA“, „MTL-FT“, „QLoRA“ und „Ours“. Die y-Achse, beschriftet mit „# FLOPs“, verwendet eine logarithmische Skala mit einem Wertebereich von 10^18 bis 10^20 und einem Tick-Intervall von 10^19. Jeder Balken repräsentiert die FLOPs für die jeweilige Methode: Der Balken für „Full FT“ ist der höchste und erreicht etwa 1,0 × 10^20 FLOPs, gefolgt von „TAG“ bei etwa 8,5 × 10^19, „LoRA“ bei etwa 7,5 × 10^19, „MTL-FT“ bei etwa 6,5 × 10^19, „QLoRA“ bei etwa 5,5 × 10^19 und „Ours“ bei etwa 5,0 × 10^19. Die ersten fünf Balken sind orange, während der letzte Balken für „Ours“ grün ist. Die Balken sind nicht sortiert, sondern in der Reihenfolge der x-Achse angeordnet. Es gibt keine visuelle Hervorhebung oder besondere Markierungen außer der Farbunterscheidung zwischen „Ours“ und den anderen Methoden.
